Is this normal?

My parents have both been with me for three weeks now to help my mom get through her radiation and chemo. I’m here all day helping. In this short time I’m noticing my dad doing things that I just can’t believe and that worry me. For example, walking away from the fridge leaving the door wide open while it’s beeping to notify it’s open, walking away from the garden hose that is on full blast and not hearing or seeing that he left it running. The other day he also hit my garage door while parking. Is this just normal cognitive decline for an 80 yr old and how do you deal when you’re scared to even leave them unattended in your home? These mishaps are practically daily and I can only imagine if I wasn’t here to catch it all as it happens.

Just another random rant

So I've been pretty angry and self pitying the last month or so. Last week I made a conscious effort to try and pull myself out of it. I spoiled myself a little,  ordered lunch from my favorite restaurant, spent time chatting about something other than my husband/my "duties" as his caregiver...

And I'm frickin exhausted. I tried, I really did, but the more I tried to be happy-fucking-sunshine the more my husband seemed to be determined to suck the joy out of existence. I put on music and start to clean, he complains, I start the vaccum, he starts yelling, I cook him lunch, he wants McDonalds,  I spend an hour making him his favorite dinner,  he hands me back the plate and again asks for McDonalds. I make him a smoothie,  he wants a cookie. He wakes me up at 3am to change the channel,  then again at 530. And all of this is done with severe aphasia so I have to play a fucked up version of 20 questions to understand exactly what it is he's complaining about. 

I have tried to be kind and patient all week,  I was loving and sweet, I made jokes, I have given kisses, I tried to be who I was before all of this, I pretended he was who he used to be, and  for a minute I believed everything was going to be ok....

Then yesterday my favorite appliance, my air fryer died, the person who was supposed to help me last night never showed, and this morning I was greeted with a diaper oozing with explosive diarrhea. 

I want out. I want to give up. I want to wake up from this nightmare. But mostly I want my partner back, the one who would try everything under the sun to make me laugh when he could see I was having a shitty day. I just want him to give 1/1000th of the effort I put in. Is that too much to ask?

Anyway,  thanks for coming to my pity party, gift bags are by the door.

Allowing parent with dementia to visit the family home they can no longer live in.

My sister and I have a parent (mother - mid 80's) who has dementia, and it has progressed to a point where residential dementia care is necessary.   Her husband (our father) passed away around 10 years ago, and she has been living in the home independently.   Incidents over the last few months (her flooding the house, not eating, not bathing, becoming highly disorientated, significant memory issues, various safety issues) lead us to having her assessed by her long term Primary Doctor (who she has seen for well over a decade) plus a separate hospital appointed provider.  We also activated her enduring power of attorney.   She has been assessed as needing residential dementia care and living at home is not an option at all.   She is physically very fit for her age and in good physical health (she will quite happily walk for 30 minutes at a time - is active in her garden for hours at a time etc.)

Added complexity I live in the US, but my mother is in New Zealand.  My sister lives very close to her in NZ (10 minutes) from our mother.

We are lucky enough that selling her home of 40+ years is not necessary.  In fact we may decide to keep her house and rent it out at some point (not in immediate term) to generate ongoing income to offset care costs. We have resources to pay for our mother's care longer term (several years at least, and possibly indefinitely if we add in rental income to the mix - our father did an excellent job setting her up for retirement.... thanks Dad where ever you are!).   Point being her home will likely be accessible for a long time to come.

**Question: As we move mom to residential dementia care, should we let her visit back to her home at all,  or is making it a clean break a better choice.**   

This has happened suddenly so she really hasn't been back since the flood - save for gathering some belongings for a few hours before repairs even started.  It seems unfair to not let her visit - it truely was a family home and she was very house proud.  Since the flood she has been at my sister's house, then a temporary residential care facility and a hospital for the assessment. We understand how it could impact her ability to adjust to a residential dementia care facility and potentially be very upsetting.   We are looking for perspectives on allowing her to return to visit could help/hurt her transition.   My sister and I can see both sides of this and are interested in other's experiences.  Mom keeps saying she wants to return home, which is heartbreaking.

For the next month as we repair the flood damage to her house, it is unlivable anyway (some asbestos ceiling materials were discovered by the insurance company's builder so there is a lot of remediation work required to remove that during repairs - luckily we had great insurance on the house.....).  We have been thinking whether taking her home to see how big the repairs are may help set the tone that returning home isn't an option.

Hey do we have words for the levels of care we give our dependants?

I both work as a professional caregiver and I take care of my disabled husband.

At work we have two different kinds of care companionate, and hands on.

Companionate care is taking care of the house and driving them places but not touching them. So no baths no transfers no doing thier hair etc. 

Hands on care can either be ONLY hands on and no housekeeping or driving but most of the time it's everything. So both companionate and hands on together.

Does this community have any other words for what level of care they give to thier dependants?

Basically if you have a word that you have a definition for list it in the comments so we can all know them.

Everything in step father's name and he won't let my mom move to safety. 

I did a search to find something similar, apologies if this has already been discussed at length. 

My question is if there is anything I can do as it seems like my mother doesn't have any rights to use to advocate for change. 

The details: 

I live in Canada.


My mom (79) and step father (82) live in their dream house in the forest about 3 hours from me. They are on acreage* in woods outside a small town. Nearest hospital is 45 min in either direction. *If anything happened to them there is likely no way to get help as if they are home alone, injured, they couldn't obvs get to a phone, and there's aren't any neighbours or friends to notice if there aren't at events or whatever. They would just die and no one would notice. 

Step dad is a stubborn chauvinist.  He insisted my mom stop working when they married and he controls everything. Their marriage is awful (my mom isn't innocent in this, she's toxic grin depression of being in this marriage for 40 years.) 

Everything is in my step father's name. House, car, investments. She does not know where the will is and he won't show it to her (gaslights her if she asks). 


She has fallen twice in the last 3 months, all due to losing her footing on logical things* and not being able to recover quickly to avoid a fall. Meaning it is not neurological decline that made her fall, but genuine tripping. (She tripped in the brick edging in one of their garden beds, or in the hose on the pathway, and finally when the dog got tangled in her legs while she was making dinner.) In all three falls he was not home. With the two outside ones she hit her head but didn't lose consciousness and eventually managed to crawl to the house and recover. Had she passed out she would have died (or at least gotten very very sick) as it was very cold and raining and he wouldn't have seen her body when he came home, due to location.  

She is not safe to continue living there but he refuses to move. His parents are buried (ashes) on the property. He built the freaking house. He has ZERO plan to ever move out any awareness that he might not be able to live there 'forever'. I cannot afford to buy the land from him so it "stays in the family" (it's worth millions). 

She would like to move to an apt near me. Community, family, living in a city with resources for her ... 

I have POA for her, we set that up about ten years ago when he refused to show her the will. But of course it just covers her health care decisions (in the event the hospital even calls me). 

I know from others who's parent has died and everything is not in both of their names, that getting access to anything (funds, accounts) can take years (is this probate?) and until that time I'd need to cover her finances (which I don't have the $ to do).  

I lie in bed thinking about what to do here and I never come up with anything. 

If I talk to him about putting things in both their names he'll say no ("she's awful with money") and he'll get mad at her for telling me how things are in their marriage. I think as her kid that I have the right to know (as does she for crying out loud) what provisions have been made in the event that he dies first. Where the will is. Who his lawyer is. What his build area like each month. Basic stuff that shouldn't be so guarded. 
 
This has been the situation for decades and I would just go round and round in my head but never do anything because of the reasons above. (I mean really, what can I "do"?). 

But now that she's fallen multiple times and luckily not had worse outcomes, and she wants to move, I feel like this need to change and things need to be said. 

But I'm pretty sure she has zero 'rights' in this situation, and without access to her own money can't leave anyway. 

Is there anything I can do that I haven't considered? 

Thanks for reading all of this.

My parents (mom 78, dad 82) are getting to that stage in life where they really can’t make good decisions for themselves. Not all the time, just some of the time. My dad has to use a walker and is basically blind, my mom’s cognitive faculties are in steep decline. They want to move closer to me so that I can start helping them out because of course they’re “not ready for a retirement home yet” (I know they’ll never be “ready”). The process of even thinking about moving has my mother so extra-stressed that they essentially haven’t even started. I’ve suggested small steps- go through the things they want to donate or sell or toss first. That’s way too much- my mom starts yelling that she can’t possibly decide. She swings from “we’ll just move everything” to “we’ll just sell everything and start over”. And they put it off more and more- it’s been about two years they’ve been talking about this move. I think they’re just one accident (like a slip and fall in the shower) away from going into a nursing home. 

On top of this my mom has become very argumentative about everything. And she’s losing weight very quickly but refuses to see a doctor (she is from the generation that brainwashed women that thin is good, so she sees it as a good thing. She is not dieting and she’s already small.) But, even me trying to suggest that she start drinking nutritional drinks is met with arguments. They too expensive. Dad drinks them all. She just forgets to buy them. Etc. 

There is no solution to this, I know. They will not listen to me, and never have. All I can do is suggest things to them and watch as they decide to stay stagnant until some emergency makes their decisions for them.

Increasing anxiety phone calls from mother

My mother, 93 with short-term memory loss, relies on me for most things at this point, and a pattern that's gone through the roof this week is odd phone calls asking if I'm OK. I rent the house next door to her, and she just called me at midnight because "your lights were still on." It's perfectly normal for my porch lights to be on at midnight. On Sunday, I went to an afternoon concert and told her I might be a little later than usual getting back to get her dinner, but emphasized that I would be there and NOT TO CALL ASKING WHERE I WAS. I emphasized that to her, and she answered, "OK." The phone calls started when I was driving home on the highway in the dark in pouring rain. I didn't feel safe answering the phone because I didn't want to take my eyes off the road (my car is too old to have Bluetooth links to a cell phone). She called three times. When I arrived home, a neighbor was sitting there with her. She had called the neighbor because she was so worried about me. I also keep a land line at home, and there were four messages on the answering machine there. 

It's getting out of control and making my life even more miserable than it already is. 

I guess it's because she lives alone with a cat, but it's like her anxieties build up until she starts imagining that something bad has happened to me and then talks herself into the idea that it has actually happened. 

Other than my constantly calling to reassure her (which I really don't want to have to do), are there any ideas on how to moderate this anxiety for her? I'm getting really angry about it.

Anyone else experience unearned distrust from your loved one?

Guys, this caregiver stuff is so freaking hard. My dad has been a widower since my mom passed in 2013. It’s been a long 11 years, full of many personality shifts in him, and mental & physical decline. My father needs a lot of help. At the same time, he is codependent along side not being able to accept his limitations, if that makes sense? 

He was born deaf, and premature. He also happens to have a low IQ, & was partially raised by foster families during the school year so he could go to deaf school. I feel his circumstances gave him no adult coping skills, no common sense, and possibly contributed to some childhood trauma. He was a great dad for the most part. He seemed more with it & intelligent in my memories of him. When I was about 15, I got emancipated. Long story short, I’m still unpacking my shit from his choices & mistakes from my upbringing. He’s a difficult man to care for, when our history is painful.

He had a difficult knee replacement, and lived in a hospital for 90 days in a neighboring town due to a terrible infection. This is the start of him sabotaging his own wellbeing and health. I stepped up. He moved into my home. It’s crowded, but manageable. But my family didn’t ask to be a part of this. I feel obligated, but in turn they have to shoulder the obligation without getting to choose. My kids & husband have been wonderful. My dad has had around 10 back surgeries total, & something like 32 surgeries in his lifetime. He played football hard in his younger years. He worked physical labor, & with his boomer mentality, working until you are in pain, and then working past that, is normal. His body is tense, solid condensed compacted muscle, fused bones, scar tissue, among other things. 

He has been forgetting he’s paid bills, & paid over, putting himself in the hole. He won’t stop buying off of Facebook, believing scam texts, going down YouTube rabbit holes & believing it all. He ours blind trust into friends who have been shitty to him. My husband & I helped him get a home equity to consolidate debt & get back on his feet. After he was maxed out, but in a better position, He went out & took out a WellsFargo loan & bought a car that he couldn’t afford that lost $25k value the day he drove it home. 

He can’t turn his neck, making driving unsafe. 
I’ve been driving that ridiculous car he’s stuck with. But lately he’s been saying he’s going to take his car, & he’s going to drive it without permission. He said he refuses to believe his body gave up on him. He falls & hurts himself by doing stupid things he knows better than doing.  He had been helping with household bills etc. We would just have him pick up our Sam’s orders, and we paid all the other bills. Everytime we would go over the purchase, and he would comprehend. 2 months later, he’s forgotten, and questioning his bank statement thinking I’ve just taken his card & stolen from him! Then he tells his friends he can’t drive his own car he paid for because his daughter is a bitch. He told my brother that my husband & I are stealing from him & he wants to move. (Absolutely no theft going on here). 

He says crazy off the wall stuff, and I am having a hard time forgiving his blatant distrust of me. My brother refuses to help or even visit. My dad spends all of his time in my home, with his grandkids. He doesn’t have to cook, clean, do laundry, take himself to appointments, feed his dog, among just a few things that we do for him. My dad has a brother who doesn’t care about my dad, screwed him in my grandparents estate, & my dad still trusts him more than I. He’s a narcissist, but also such a basic human. He throws fits like a teen & uses the DARVO method. Such as making statements like “I wish I could be in heaven with my wife,” “I’m just deaf and dumb dad”, or “people know I been like this forever, I never change.” I have to remind him that his wife, is my mom. I lost her too. Why does he blindly trust people who let him down, but distrust & tear down me & my family who care for him the most? Anyone else experience this with their parent? 

TL/DR
Deaf, disabled, dumb dad is ungrateful, trusts strangers, but distrusts me, his only caregiver & family member that talks to him.

Relative didn’t sign her will…

TLDR; relative didn’t sign her will and now my parent in the nursing home is being punished. 

Hi guys, I was a pretty active member of this sub until my parent transitioned to long term care last year, but I wanted to tell a cautionary tale. And I want to vent. 

Over the past two years, my mom’s sister has been talking to me about what she’s going to leave me in her will. She was going to leave me everything; life changing money. She died suddenly yesterday. 

Here comes the greedy relative part. Right? Not really. 

When she passed I made a quick call to the lawyer because there was something I need immediate information on (it was pet related). I’m the course of the conversation, they mentioned that I was her beneficiary—but as the title says, NEVER SIGNED THE WILL. 

This means that her asset will immediately transfer to her next of kin, my mom. Cool, right? Mom will get some extra cash, live like a princess and probably gift a few bucks to me. 

No. Mom is on Medicaid. So in essence, my Aunt worked her entire life only for the state to come in and take it. But it gets worse. Because of this increase in assets, mom will actually get kicked off Medicaid and have to go through the whole process again. 

The real kicker? She got a letter in the mail the day she went back into the hospital letting her know her will was never signed. 

I am so angry. She would have been better off leaving her entire estate to charity. My feelings aside, she would have never wanted to harm her sister financially. What a mess. 

Anyway, thank you for reading if you’ve gotten this far. Please, please check your loved ones documents. No matter what they said and promised, they are elderly and the system is stacked against them.

Could severe dry mouth be from Parkinson’s, the meds, or a reaction to stopping Lansoprazole?

Since returning to his old meds, he’s experiencing extremely dry mouth — much worse than before, to the point where his gums feel like they’re sticking to his tongue. He’s well hydrated, so it doesn’t seem like dehydration.

Has anyone else dealt with this level of dryness? Could it be Parkinson’s, the meds, or possibly the reflux treatment making things worse? Any experiences or advice would be hugely appreciated.

resentment and anger and venting and ARRRGH!!!

Hi there, I've never posted on here but reading others stories has made me feel like i'm not terrible for the resentment I feel. this post will probably be loong and rambling but I need to feel like im getting this out of my head.  

I've been caring for my mom in one capacity or another for almost 9 years. a lot of the time it had to do with her taking on responsibility that she was not physically capable of carrying out. like looking after my nieces while my brother and his wife worked..basically full time child care of 2, then 3 then 4 children. I was the only one who could physically lift the kids.. i took them to and from pre k, met with the teachers,babysat the infants etc etc..she and I did this together and as the kids got older and needed less of my day to day care, my mother needed more.. a seamless transition from one to the other it seems!  

over these past years we've always lived in a two family home or something similar..so i could be close by to help her if needed. now we're living together in a small apartment. my husband and I and my Mom. she has had mobility issues and some other concerns that have been pretty constant and increasingly limited. it's one thing after another. she's needed extra help for a lot of things for a long time but was semi independent to varying degrees up until recently. 

on thanksgiving 2025 she had a stroke and had to go into rehab for about a month. I was so relieved to get a break! and I also felt she was finally getting a better level of care. however,even though she was not at home it was still a lot for me.. she was emotional and called me through the night when she was upset with staff. had some delerium off and on.. seeing things and getting paranoid.. i visited about 3-4 times a week, advocated for her anytime i felt she wasn't getting something she needed and for her comfort..the rehab was not fancy but it was a quality program and the people were caring and upright. unfortunately the last appeal we made to fight her insurance trying to discharge her was lost. She was discharged in considerably worse condition than before the stroke. now she is home with only me. she needs help with everything..can only walk on a walker for very short distances. she complains a lot of  the time..gets dismayed and falls into despair over almost every move from the bed to the bathroom..etc.I know she's frustrated. she cries whenever I leave the house. calls me way too much when i do, for unnecessary  things..guilt trips me. the other day had a full on tantrum while I was helping her getting into bed out of anger and frustration that I had left earlier. wakes me up several times a night. I never know if its an actual need( going to the bathroom) or something that absolutely didn't need to be dealt with at 3 30 am.. (where is my scarf?) I've told her I need sleep, I make sure she has what she needs at arms reach for the night. after my request I'll get one night of full sleep, then it's right back to calling regardless of the time. more often than not our nights are full of interrupted sleep, her loud wailing and crying ..and wanting to have these conversations about how frustrated she is about her condition after having woken me up out of a dead sleep at 3:15 am.. then angry and guilt trippy when i'm not up for it and want to go lay down..she is very impatient with any requests.. calling out "Hello? Childcare and Eldercare are not the same at all

How many times have we heard that our parents took care of us and we owe it to take care of them.  Whereas it is our duty to make sure they are taken care in their old age (although they should be responsible enough to prepare if they can),  it is nothing like taking care of a baby or toddler.  

Babies grow and develop life skills such as walking, eating on their own, using the toilet , dresses themselves, etc.  In a few years , they start school, make friends and become a little less dependent on their parents (they learn to play with others and entertain themselves.    Parents are also most likely a lot younger and have more energy when they have children than when they become caregivers.  You don't see very many 60 year old mothers with small children. 

Elderly parents with dementia are going to the opposite direction.  The become less social and need more and more help.    You either can't go anywhere or you have to hire a caregiver to watch them, with a baby, you can hire a teenager you know. More people are willing to take care of a cute baby than a 100 plus pound dementia person that is often resistant and difficult.  Changing a baby diaper is nothing compared to trying to change an adult.    

And most important, when a baby or toddler falls down, they might cry but they will get up and continue walking. When and old person falls, the break a bone, end up in the hospital and require more care.      Whereas we need to make sure our elderly parents are taken care , comparing it to them taking care us as babies (they brought us into the world, we didn't bring them into the world)  is very wrong.
